solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Flatter and quite insipid?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a verb, to coax with flattery
second meaning, read as a made-up word: fairly bland, with -ish meaning 'somewhat'

explanation.surface: Someone's compliments are flattering but rather dull.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer into BLAND + ISH, the suffix that softens a word to 'quite'; the question mark flags the invented word.
explanation.definitionFit: To blandish is to coax someone with flattering talk, a dated verb still used in writing.

clue.text: Reason for yawning in bedroom, shattered

indicators.note: shattered means broken into pieces, so the letters are reassembled differently

explanation.surface: Someone yawns in the bedroom because they are exhausted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shattered' is British slang for exhausted, which explains the yawning in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Boredom makes people yawn, so it is a cause of yawning.

clue.text: Good way beyond an acutely anxious feeling

indicators.note: beyond means further on, so these pieces come after the word that follows

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for good
St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: Something good lies past a sharp worry.
explanation.definitionFit: Angst is intense anxiety or dread, a word borrowed from German.

clue.text: Thought democratic elections initially freeing

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the leading letters of the two words are taken

parts.note: the opening letters of democratic and elections
liberation is the act of freeing

explanation.surface: Free elections were thoughtfully considered from the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliberation is careful consideration, a noun for thought given to something.

clue.text: Put up with firm opinion

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a verb, to tolerate
second meaning: a noun, a position taken on an issue

explanation.surface: Someone tolerates a strongly held view.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand something is to tolerate it, and to take a stand is to hold a firm position.

clue.text: Stronghold was involved in battle, it's said

indicators.note: something said is heard rather than read, so we want a word sounding like the phrase

parts.note: to be involved in a battle is to have fought; in non-rhotic British speech the two words sound the same

explanation.surface: A castle was the scene of fighting, according to the story.
explanation.definitionFit: A fort is a fortified military building, a synonym of stronghold.

clue.text: Openest, wild dance

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: The most uninhibited and frenzied dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: The one-step is a ballroom dance of the early twentieth century, an example of a dance.

clue.text: Spike Milligan finally overcome by God

indicators.note: in a down answer, overcome by means placed underneath, so this piece goes after the god

parts.note: Thor is the Norse god of thunder

indicators.note: finally means at the end, so only the closing letter of the surname is taken

explanation.surface: The comedian Spike Milligan was eventually conquered by God.
explanation.walkthrough: Spike Milligan was a British comedian of the Goon Show; here 'Spike' is detached from his surname to be the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A thorn is a sharp spike on the stem of a plant.

clue.text: Coloured panels where terribly sad angels sit

indicators.note: terribly suggests something done badly, so the letters are put into a jumbled order

explanation.surface: Church windows where mournful angels are pictured sitting.
explanation.definitionFit: Stained glass is glass coloured for decorative windows, made up of many small panels.

clue.text: Magnificent beer knocked back

indicators.note: knocked back suggests something sent backwards, so the word is read from its end

parts.note: lager is a type of beer

explanation.surface: A splendid pint was downed in one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocked back' looks like drinking the beer, which fits the surface; cryptically it turns the word round.
explanation.definitionFit: Regal means kingly, and so splendid or magnificent in appearance.

clue.text: Design of road etc, old style

indicators.note: a design is an arrangement, so these words call for the following letters to be laid out anew

explanation.surface: Planning a road and the like in an old-fashioned way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Design' looks like the definition, which fits Art Deco well, but it is the signal; the answer is defined as 'old style'.
explanation.definitionFit: Art Deco is a decorative style of the 1920s and 1930s, so an old style of design.

clue.text: Full stop, perhaps, a little period otherwise

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a full stop is one example of a small round mark
second meaning: 'period' is otherwise the name for a full stop, and the mark is a tiny spot

explanation.surface: A sentence ends with a brief pause, or another short break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Period' tempts you to think of time, but it is the American name for a full stop, so both halves describe the same small mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A dot is a small round mark, which is what a full stop or period looks like on the page.

clue.text: Wicked chap who made pots in game

parts.note: Thomas Minton founded the Minton pottery firm in Stoke-on-Trent

explanation.surface: A villainous potter appears in a game.
explanation.walkthrough: Minton is a famous English pottery maker, named after its founder Thomas Minton.
explanation.definitionFit: Badminton is a racket sport played with a shuttlecock, so an example of a game.

clue.text: Contemporary colour back in the day

indicators.note: in places the turned colour inside the word for the day

parts.note: Mon is the abbreviation for Monday

indicators.note: back means turned the other way, so the colour word is read from its end

explanation.surface: A modern shade that was fashionable long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back in the day' reads as the idiom for 'in the old days', the opposite of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Contemporary and modern are synonyms, both meaning belonging to the present time.

clue.text: Current drink

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a current of air through a room
second meaning: a single swallow of liquid

explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' reads as an adjective meaning present-day, but it is the noun for a flow of air.
explanation.definitionFit: A draught is a flow of cold air indoors, and also a gulp of something to drink.

clue.text: Moderate rage

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a verb, to tone down or soften
second meaning: a noun, an outburst of anger

explanation.surface: Fury that is only mild.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moderate' reads as an adjective on rage, but it is a verb in its own right.
explanation.definitionFit: To temper something is to soften it, and a temper is a fit of anger.

clue.text: Have due regard for holding opening of parliament in secret, surprisingly

indicators.note: holding means keeping inside, so one piece goes within the other
surprisingly hints at an unexpected outcome, so the letters come out in an unforeseen order
an opening is a beginning, so just the leading letter of the next word is used

explanation.surface: Honour the opening of parliament, held unexpectedly behind closed doors.
explanation.definitionFit: To respect someone is to hold them in high esteem, giving them the regard they are due.

clue.text: Incredible bird carrying first of twigs

indicators.note: a bird carrying something holds it inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a starling is a common bird

indicators.note: first of means just the opening letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: An amazing bird flies off with a twig for its nest.
explanation.definitionFit: Startling means astonishing or surprising, close in sense to incredible.

clue.text: Vessel briefly transporting American food from the Far East

indicators.note: a vessel transporting something carries it inside, so one piece sits within the other
briefly means cut short, so the last letter of the word is dropped

explanation.surface: A ship carries US-bound cargo of oriental food.
explanation.definitionFit: Sushi is a Japanese dish of vinegared rice, a food from the Far East.

clue.text: Country where that object lay abandoned

parts.note: it is the pronoun for that object

indicators.note: abandoned means wild and unrestrained, so the letters are let loose into a new order

explanation.surface: A country where something was left lying deserted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abandoned' reads as left behind, but cryptically it means unrestrained.
explanation.definitionFit: Italy is a country in southern Europe.

clue.text: Family member in siblings, I sense

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the following words, running across them

parts.note: the last letter of siblings, then I, then the first letter of sense

explanation.surface: Someone senses a relative among their brothers and sisters.
explanation.definitionFit: Sis is the informal short form of sister, a member of the family.

clue.text: Smart police operation

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a verb, to hurt with a sharp pain
second meaning: an undercover trap set by police

explanation.walkthrough: 'Smart' reads as clever or well dressed, but here it is the verb for a sharp pain.
explanation.definitionFit: A wound may sting or smart with pain, and a sting is an undercover police trap to catch criminals.

clue.text: Young lady soaring all over the place

indicators.note: all over the place means scattered and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A girl is flying in every direction.
explanation.walkthrough: Strictly a signora is a married Italian woman, signorina being the young one, so the definition is loose.
explanation.definitionFit: Signora is the Italian title and term for a lady or married woman.

clue.text: A team, out of the way

parts.note: a side is a sports team

explanation.surface: A sports team kept out of the way.
explanation.definitionFit: Aside is an adverb meaning to one side, out of people's path.

clue.text: Little bit I love that's much appreciated

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O
ta is British informal for thank you

explanation.surface: Someone says that a little love goes a long way.
explanation.definitionFit: Iota, a Greek letter, is used to mean a very small amount.

clue.text: Certainly overwhelmed by figure, sensing ability?

indicators.note: overwhelmed by means engulfed, so the first word is swallowed inside the second

parts.note: eight is a number, or figure

explanation.surface: Someone's shape is a sure sign of keen senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyesight is the faculty of seeing, one of the abilities by which we sense the world.
